scope: One quarantined A10 bootstrap and hardware/network/GPU readiness validation only; no public inference or arbitrary tenant workloads.
limitations: Conditional experiment risk acceptance; vulnerable dependencies are retained and are not production security certification.

Kernel package/header CVEs cannot prove running-host applicability. Ubuntu GA 6.8.0-147 remains an experimental preparation baseline with known unresolved advisories; only trusted project administration and fixed validation workloads are permitted.
GPU memory, CUDA, networking, DCGM freshness and the actual host kernel must pass separate live checks.
Public serving/gateway/model images require their own review and validation before exposing inference.
Changed locks, boundaries, images, native findings, file inventory or expiry require a new review.

rationale.reason: The verifier denylist is outdated. Only fixed Kubernetes and public registry/package origins are used; no caller-selected certificate chain or arbitrary URL is accepted. Public upstream or trust-store compromise remains a risk; these dependencies are not declared fixed.
No GPU operand or containerd listener serves caller-selected files through Go FileServer/ServeFile/ServeContent. Metrics/health ingress remains private. The affected library is retained.

HTTP/2 and gRPC peers are restricted to the private Kubernetes API, trusted local runtime sockets and operator namespace endpoints. There is no public operand/runtime API. A compromised authenticated peer can still cause denial of service; this is a bounded single-node experiment, not immunity.

No public Go TLS server or caller-supplied ECH handshake is accepted by the configured GPU/runtime components. Private metrics/health and local sockets remain restricted. Exposing a TLS listener invalidates this scope.

rationale: All attributed findings belong to the exact linux-libc-dev userspace header package: its complete native inventory contains only /usr/include/*.h and package documentation. These files do not contain the affected running kernel implementations. This is a component-applicability decision, not a repaired kernel or a waiver of running-host risks. The host independently requires the pinned GA kernel/package identities, disabled GCOV, Nouveau exclusion, root-only administration, restricted SSH, host firewall, quarantine and bounded lease. Raw findings remain retained.

rationale.reason: The driver bootstrap does not accept user-supplied Brotli content. Its package/kernel inputs use fixed distribution repositories. The decoder remains present; an upstream compromise or added Brotli input invalidates this applicability decision.
Configured operands and runtime do not use DTLS. Driver downloads use HTTPS/TCP; the installed OpenSSL implementation remains vulnerable when used for the affected DTLS operation.

The host runtime accepts no submitted RSA private JWK or configurable JWK URL. Registry authentication is fixed by the operator; CRI and containerd sockets remain host-local. Parsing arbitrary JWK material is outside the permitted profile.

The affected DNS parser remains present. Runtime registry lookups use the configured trusted host resolver and fixed registries; arbitrary tenant DNS inputs are not admitted. A compromised resolver can still deny service.

The prebuilt runtime does not fetch/build Go modules or contact a Go module proxy/checksum service on the GPU host. Module build-time compromise is not ruled out by this runtime applicability decision.
No Go module proxy or sumdb operation runs in the admitted host runtime. The reviewed binaries are checksum-pinned upstream artifacts; build-chain assurance remains an upstream dependency.

The affected s2.NewDict/Dict.Encode path is not used for submitted dictionaries. Only pinned registry artifacts are installed; no arbitrary tenant image or dictionary is accepted. Compromised upstream artifacts remain a risk.
